name: Mog Ruith

attributes.attribute: name means the slave of the wheel
met Simon Magus and attacked the head of John the Baptist
the father of Tlachtga and chief of Munster druids

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Mog Ruith, also called Mug Ruith, is an Irish hero. His name means the slave of the wheel. He was a druid who used a wheel as a tool of divination. The medieval tales send him to the eastern Mediterranean, where he met Simon Magus, a great magician. There he obeyed King Herod's command to cut off the head of John the Baptist. For this ancient crime of Mog Ruith, the Irish are said to have suffered famine and other tragedies. Some texts make him the father of the mysterious Tlachtga, a figure for whom a great site is named. He is described as Munster's chief druid, who saved its warriors in battle. He drilled a well with an arrow or spear and built a fire from the wood of magical rowan trees. In a bird cloak he flew into the air and did battle with the opposing druids.
